title: personal-okr-weekly-checkin-maya-singh-2026-03-27
content:
Weekly OKR check-in - raw notes / scratchpad

Date: 2026-03-27
Owner: Maya Singh

Objective 1: Reduce 95th percentile generation latency for hosted-api by 20% vs baseline
- Key results: 95p latency down from 420ms -> target 336ms; p50 target also -10%
- This week: rolled out smaller batching window (50ms) to 10% of traffic; initial metrics show 95p improved from 420 -> 390 on canary traffic (good signal but noisy).
- Notes: improvement concentrated on seq length < 128. For long sequences, KV cache misses still dominate.
- Next actions: expand canary to 25% if no error regressions; instrument end-to-end traces for long-seq path.
- Blockers: need infra approval for increased cache memory on dedicated nodes (ticket JIRA-5789 pending), and we still have flaky per-token tracing that drops spans (~5% of requests).

Objective 2: Improve self-serve onboarding completion rate from 45% -> 65%
- This week: A/B test of simplified quickstart reduced friction: onboarding completion for variant A is 53% (vs 47% control) — promising.
- Action: follow up with UX to iron out error messages for rate-limit responses; add explicit next steps in email flow.

Personal growth / learning goals
- Spend 2 hours/week on distributed tracing deep dive (started tutorial on OpenTelemetry) — completed 1.5h this week.
- Pair with Priya on canary rollout checklist (scheduled Mon).

Retro / What worked
- Smaller batching window gave immediate measurable benefit for short requests — good quick win.
- Cross-team sync with SRE helped unblock a config change faster than expected.

Retro / What to improve
- Need better signal on long-tail requests. Current dashboards smooth out spikes; want raw histogram export for sequences >512 tokens.
- Testing infra for tracing needs a reproducible test harness. TODO: prod-like replay for tracing tests.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Question: Is there an easy way to route long-seq traffic to nodes with warmer KV caches? Could be a routing policy tweak. Ask infra/serving-runtime.
- TODO: follow up on JIRA-5789 (cache memory increase) — ping infra on Mon if no update.
- TODO: write short doc on "when to prefer smaller batching window vs cache sizing" for the team (draft by Apr 3).

Quick wins to try next week
- Expand 50ms window canary to 25% (if no errors).
- Add histogram export for seq length >512 to debug dashboard (follow up with observability).
- Draft onboarding email copy with explicit next steps and share w/ growth.

Links and refs (scratch)
- Confluence: model-latency-playbook (CONFLUENCE-1234)
- Jira: JIRA-5789, JIRA-5820 (tracing reliability)
- Slack threads: #serving-runtime thread 03/24 "batching tweak results"

Notes to self (personal)
- Keep notes terse in this doc; move polished summary to shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/one-pager when ready.
- Remember to capture A/B test variant definitions in the experiment tracker before expanding canary.

End of check-in.
summary: Short weekly personal OKR/check-in for Maya Singh covering latency objective progress, onboarding KR, blockers (cache mem approval + tracing flakiness), next steps, and personal learning goals.
